thesis: SPY is just below its record and VIX is at a six-month low of 14.25 going into two Fed events inside the window: the FOMC minutes on Wednesday and Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote at about 10 AM Friday. A retail earnings run (HD/LOW/TGT/WMT) also lands days after a -0.6% retail-sales print, so the Council's stance is to keep cash ready and put no size into binary events. The book only takes setups the repo shows as live: the confirmed XLF breakout through JPM, healthcare's all-time-high rotation through MRK, and tech through MSFT rather than NVDA ahead of its Aug 26 print. CVX and LMT are small hedges against what the Council names as its biggest risk: Hormuz-driven oil rising while the consumer weakens. Five sectors, no earnings reports inside the window and 20% cash keep beta near 0.6, which respects the concentration scar and stays close to the ~25% cash stance while the risk register is still green.
risks: A dovish Warsh plus a clean WMT print could lift tech and cyclicals sharply and leave this low-beta, 20%-cash book behind SPY; a US-Iran de-escalation would hit CVX and LMT together, and a hawkish, oil-citing debut would hit JPM and MSFT at the same time. I have no memory of how this week played out (my training data ends months before it), so none of this draws on hindsight.
